reason: Driven end to end on BOTH grounds with a stubbed clipboard, on both entry paths, and it reproduces exactly as both wordings state. (A) First-run path, ?v=paper and ?v=ink, state=owner-empty: type '3 October 2026', Set the day, Add a moment, name it, Escape -> owner-flight reads 'Only you can see this' / verb 'Publish' / 'Updated 16 July 2026'. Publish -> 'Send it to Aisling & Tom.' Copy the link -> the live token genuinely reaches the clipboard (https://timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM), the button reads 'Copied', .b-live says 'Link copied.', and .b-pressTitle does not move. Back to the plan -> 'Only you can see this', verb 'Publish', stamp 'Updated 16 July 2026'. Pressing Publish again lands on 'Send it to Aisling & Tom.' (B) state=owner-draft, identical on paper and ink: after Copy and Back the plan still reads 'Only you can see this' / 'Publish' / 'Updated 16 July 2026'. The mechanism is exactly as named. grep of every F.publication reference in render-b.js, fixture.js and render-core.js gives ONE draft->published write in the whole product, render-b.js:1278-1279, inside wireOwner's `copy` branch; wireOwner is called only from ownerSurface (:1503), and the only [data-act="copy"] control in the artifact is render-b.js:1802, on states.publish, whose own handler (:1809-1825) sets the button label and the live line and never touches the record. So the branch is dead and the product has no publish transition at all: three writers set the record to DRAFT (:1249 add-a-moment, :1564 owner-draft, :1615 first-run) and none set it to published. paintPublication does not run late from a stale read - it never runs on this path. The published wording ('Live since 15 July - anyone with the link can read it', 'Get the link', 'Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.') is reachable only because fixture.js:182 seeds publication as published; no plan built through the product ever leaves draft, and 'You can turn the link off at any time' promises an on/off state the product never enters. Not already handled: round 9's confirmed brand--draft-publishes-a-date-before-the-draft shipped only half its sharpened fix - part (1), owner-draft committing the draft record, is in the code at :1564; part (2), moving the flip into the states.publish copy handler, is not, and both round-9 refuters flagged it in as many words as a SEPARATE live defect ('the flip is unreachable dead code today'). Not SETTLED: the only neighbouring entry, draft-branch-restored-before-it-is-used, was refuted on the stash/restore in the owner-draft builder, a different mechanism that has since been changed. Not a gate restatement: interaction-check.mjs's single publication assertion (:2626) tests the verb against the STATIC fixture record at load on owner-flight and asserts nothing about copy, and audit.mjs measures no string. No constraint touched - no colour, no weight, no architecture, and it is not the data model but the surface's own stated model, written verbatim in the code at :1275-1277. I simulated the proposed fix in-page and drove it on both grounds: Copy flips the heading to 'Mara & Finn have had this since 16 July.' in place, Back to the plan reads 'Live since 16 July - anyone with the link can read it' with verb 'Get the link' and stamp 'Updated 16 July 2026', and Publish again correctly lands on the published heading. It is a correction of about twenty lines, no new state, and it removes a duplicate writer rather than adding one. Real at a 9.5 bar: the single question the owner of a wedding asks this screen - have they got it - is answered 'Only you can see this' forever.
sharpenedFix: Do exactly what the finding says, with three notes from driving it. (1) Put the flip in a single takeTheLink() and call it from the writeText success callback in states.publish (render-b.js:1810-1817), BEFORE action.textContent = 'Copied', then rewrite .b-pressTitle from the same accessor that built it at :1774-1776 so the screen the owner is standing on changes under them; delete the dead branch at render-b.js:1275-1282 so there is one writer. paintPublication then picks up the status line, the verb and the stamp on the next go('owner-flight') with no extra call - verified. (2) The heading rewrite is silent to assistive tech: go() focuses .b-pressTitle with tabindex=-1, and changing the text of the already-focused node announces nothing. The .b-live region on that screen is already firing 'Link copied.' - extend that one existing string to also state the new fact (e.g. 'Link copied. Anyone holding it can read the plan.'), which is the only place the flip is announced at all. That costs one string; leaving it silent costs the whole state change for a screen-reader owner. (3) Scope the mutation the way round 9 warned: console.html switches state in place with no reload, so a committed record persists across a picker change. The first-run and owner-draft paths already commit, so this adds nothing new in kind, but if the seam is ever closed it should be closed once in C.setState rather than by restoring inside a builder. Re-run interaction-check.mjs after: its only publication assertion reads the static fixture on owner-flight and is untouched by this, but the gate should gain one assertion that Copy the link flips the owner surface, or this exact defect can regress silently again.
